overview: Jamaica is an island country in the Caribbean, south of Cuba. Its capital and largest city is Kingston. Jamaica became independent from the United Kingdom in 1962. It is the birthplace of reggae music and Bob Marley, and its sprinters, including Usain Bolt, have won many Olympic medals.

geography.text: Jamaica is the third-largest island in the Caribbean. Mountains run along the middle of the island, and the Blue Mountains in the east, where a famous coffee is grown, are the highest. Much of the island is limestone, with caves and underground rivers, and its coast is lined with beaches.

history.text: Jamaica's Taíno people were wiped out after Spain arrived in 1494. Britain captured the island in 1655 and turned it into a major sugar colony worked by enslaved Africans, while people who escaped, known as Maroons, formed free communities in the mountains. Slavery ended in 1834, and Jamaica became independent in 1962.

events.title: Maroon treaty
events.text: The British sign a treaty recognising Maroon communities.
